title: Support, resistance and consolidation
summary: Support and resistance are zones where price has turned before. A consolidation is a sideways box between them, often after a bigger move.
unreliableWhen: Levels are zones, not exact lines, and every chart shows some level if you look hard enough. A box drawn after the fact always looks neat. Price can leave a consolidation either way.
goodExample: Drawing a zone through three earlier turns at 1.0848–1.0855 and noting the box is about 2 ATR tall.
badExample: Drawing a new line at every wick until the chart is full of lines, or expecting a level to hold because it held before.

chart.lookFor: Use the Zone tool to mark the top and bottom of the range where price turned at least twice. Compare the box height with ATR 14 in the lower pane.
